office_does: One of two Washington State Representatives for the 45th District (Kirkland, Redmond, Woodinville, Sammamish, Duvall), serving two-year terms writing state law and budgets.
race_blurb: Open seat after Rep. Larry Springer's retirement. Redmond City Councilmember Vanessa Kritzer, who took 62.75% in the primary, faces Republican John P Gibbons, who filed no pamphlet statement or biography and reports no fundraising.

candidates.summary: Redmond City Councilmember since 2020 and former Council President; executive director of the Washington Association of Land Trusts.
highlights: Supports progressive revenue, including recent taxes on high earners, and is open to an income tax [S5]
Raised Redmond's inclusionary-zoning requirements and created a renter-protections code chapter [S5]
Says "the state should set the floor" on housing, with cities choosing how to meet it [S5]
Lists support for reproductive rights and LGBTQIA+ protections [S3]

taxes.basis: Calls the tax code deeply regressive, supports taxing high earners and is open to an income tax; cites Redmond's head tax.

spending.basis: Would fully fund education, restore childcare and early-learning cuts, and use progressive revenue for sustained investment.

housing.basis: Record on inclusionary zoning, supportive housing and renter protections; supports state rent stabilization, alongside supply-oriented planning.

climate.basis: Calls climate action a moral imperative; record includes Redmond's sustainability plan, net-zero strategy and CCA-funded electric fire engines.

experience.basis: Six-plus years on the Redmond council including Council President; no state legislative record.

local-control.basis: "The state should set the floor" on housing production and affordability, with local flexibility on implementation.

immigration.basis: Secured local funding for immigrant and refugee services and backed a resolution on constitutional protections.

social.basis: Lists standing up for reproductive rights and passing policies affirming LGBTQIA+ rights; supports stronger state anti-discrimination protections.

candidates.summary: Republican candidate who submitted no statement, biography or photo to the voters' pamphlet and lists no campaign website.
highlights: No pamphlet statement or biography submitted [S1]
No PDC financial reports on file as of September 17 [S3]
